tasks.prompt: During smoke testing in a prairie city, a new crew reports every roof vent on a street as a defect, filling the log with false findings.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian smoke and dye investigation. Test conditions and results are as stated.

evidence.label: Smoke discharging from roof plumbing vents is the expected path for smoke in a sound system.
No smoke appears at ground level, cracks, or cleanouts on the street.
Dye and flow records for the street show no unusual storm response.
An experienced operator reviewing the log finds no ground level smoke photographs.
At one home, smoke also came from a dry trap indoors, separately noted by the crew.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The vent reports are normal smoke behaviour, not defects, and the log needs correction and crew coaching
Every home on the street has a defective vent connection to repair
The sewer is leaking into every home on the street
Smoke testing should be cancelled because vents discharge smoke

inference.explanation: Vent discharge is the designed smoke path, no ground smoke was photographed, and flow data is quiet. The real finding on the street was the single dry trap, not a street of defects.

nextClue.prompt: Which quality step best protects future test results?

options.label: Coach crews on expected vent discharge versus defect smoke, and require ground level photographs for defect entries
Send repair notices to every home in the log
Delete smoke testing from the program entirely

nextClue.explanation: Training plus photographic evidence keeps defect logs trustworthy.

clueText.nc-a: The program adds a vent versus defect briefing and a photo requirement for every defect entry.
clueText.nc-b: Notices based on normal vent behaviour would alarm residents and waste follow up resources.
clueText.nc-c: One misread log does not invalidate a method that works when read correctly.

tasks.prompt: A duplex lift station in Regina shows Pump 1 delivering steadily less flow over six months while Pump 2 holds its rate.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Drawdown tests show Pump 1 at 62 percent of its rated flow and Pump 2 at 97 percent, tested the same week.
Pump 1 motor current and discharge pressure are near normal for its speed.
Measured impeller to wear ring clearance on Pump 1 is about twice the maker limit, found at inspection.
Both pumps share the same wet well, force main and discharge conditions.
Swapping the duty order does not change which pump delivers less.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The shared force main is blocking and reducing both pumps equally
Pump 1 internal wear, shown by the excessive impeller clearance, is recirculating flow and cutting its output
Pump 2 is oversized and making Pump 1 look weak by comparison
The wet well level floats are set wrong for Pump 1 only

inference.explanation: A shared discharge path rules out a common blockage, current is normal, and the measured clearance gives a physical cause inside Pump 1 alone.

nextClue.prompt: Which repair decision best follows from the inspection?

options.label: Clean the shared force main as the first action
Rebuild or replace the worn impeller and wear ring on Pump 1, then repeat the drawdown test
Replace both pumps because one is worn

nextClue.explanation: Repairing the measured wear and retesting verifies the fix on the affected pump only.

clueText.nc-a: The force main serves the healthy pump at full rate, so it is not the first suspect.
clueText.nc-b: After the rebuild, Pump 1 drawdown returns to 96 percent of rated flow.
clueText.nc-c: Pump 2 tests at 97 percent, so replacing it is not supported.

tasks.prompt: Both pumps at a Saskatoon lift station lose capacity over one week, and discharge pressure at the pumps reads higher than normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Both pumps show the same capacity loss in drawdown tests.
Discharge pressure at the station is well above its normal value at the same flows.
A discharge valve downstream is found about three quarters closed after recent work nearby.
Pump inspections show impellers and clearances in good condition on both pumps.
Reopening the valve fully restores normal pressure and full drawdown rates the same day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both pump impellers wore out in the same week
The force main collapsed somewhere downstream
The partly closed discharge valve throttled the station and raised its operating head
Air in the wet well reduced both pumps output

inference.explanation: A common cause affecting both healthy pumps, high pressure, a found throttled valve, and instant recovery on reopening identify the valve, not the pumps.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best prevents a repeat after nearby work?

options.label: Schedule both pumps for rebuild each year
Install larger motors to push through throttled valves
Add a valve position check to the return to service checklist after any work near the station discharge

nextClue.explanation: A position check catches the exact failure mode that caused this event.

clueText.nc-a: Annual rebuilds do not address a valve left partly closed.
clueText.nc-b: Larger motors mask a throttling fault and raise energy and surge risk.
clueText.nc-c: The checklist now requires confirming full open position and normal discharge pressure before leaving site.

tasks.prompt: A lift station wet well in a mountain town grows a thick grease mat that coats its floats, and pump behaviour becomes erratic.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Pumps start late and stop early at random levels through the week.
A grease mat several centimetres thick floats on the wet well and coats the float switches.
Manual drawdown tests with floats held clear show both pumps at full rated flow.
Upstream of the station is a restaurant strip with a history of grease discharge.
After the mat is vacuumed out and floats cleaned, level control returns to normal for the test week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both pump motors are failing intermittently
The station control panel has a faulty starter on both pumps
The force main is air locked and confusing the level control
The grease mat fouling the floats is causing the erratic control, while the pumps themselves are sound

inference.explanation: Full flow on manual test, a mat coating the controls, and normal operation after cleaning isolate the mat as the cause and clear the pumps and panel.

nextClue.prompt: Which program step best follows for this station?

options.label: Add scheduled wet well grease removal and an upstream grease source follow up for the restaurant strip
Replace both pump starters as a precaution
Raise the float levels so the mat matters less

nextClue.explanation: Removing the recurring mat and addressing its source treats the cause, not the symptom.

clueText.nc-a: The station joins a grease watch list with scheduled vacuuming, and the strip premises are flagged for interceptor checks.
clueText.nc-b: Starters tested fine under manual control, so replacing them is not supported.
clueText.nc-c: Raising floats narrows the working range and can worsen cycling and overflow risk.

tasks.prompt: A force main station in Alberta loses capacity and surges after its high point air release valve is found fouled shut.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Station capacity falls gradually and discharge pressure swings during each pump run.
The air release valve at the force main high point is fouled with grit and grease and does not open.
A temporary vent opened at the high point releases a large volume of air during a pump run.
Pump drawdown at the wet well end is normal when the force main is vented manually.
No change in pump condition is found at inspection, and the wet well is clean.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Air accumulating at the high point because the release valve failed is restricting the force main
Both pumps have lost impeller efficiency at the same time
The force main is partly blocked by a solid obstruction at its low point
The wet well is too small and starves the pumps of flow

inference.explanation: Pressure swings, a fouled valve, a large air release on venting, and normal vented performance identify trapped air. A solid blockage would not clear by venting air.

nextClue.prompt: Which maintenance step best prevents recurrence?

options.label: Replace both pumps with higher head models
Put high point air release valves on a scheduled inspection and cleaning cycle
Lower the wet well operating levels permanently

nextClue.explanation: Servicing the valves that failed keeps the air path open.

clueText.nc-a: Higher head pumps would fight trapped air at higher energy cost without removing it.
clueText.nc-b: Air release valves are added to the quarterly station rounds with a function check.
clueText.nc-c: Wet well levels do not control air collecting at a force main high point.

tasks.prompt: Run hours at a duplex station in Brandon climb steadily, yet pumped volumes do not, and the wet well rises whenever a pump stops.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Total pump run hours rise about 25 percent over two months with no rise in station inflow.
The wet well level rises noticeably in the minutes after Pump 1 stops, with no inflow change.
A flow check on the Pump 1 discharge shows reverse flow when that pump is off.
Pump 2 shows no reverse flow and its stop leaves the level steady.
Drawdown rate while Pump 1 runs is near normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Station inflow has grown by 25 percent without any billing change
Pump 1 check valve is leaking back, so part of its output recirculates and inflates run hours
Both pumps are wearing out together and losing efficiency
The level floats are calling for extra runs with no water present

inference.explanation: Reverse flow on one pump only, level rising after it stops, and normal running performance identify a leaking check valve recirculating pumped flow.

nextClue.prompt: Which repair best matches the finding?

options.label: Replace both pumps because run hours are up
Enlarge the wet well to hold the extra volume
Repair or replace the Pump 1 check valve and confirm no reverse flow after shutdown

nextClue.explanation: Fixing the leaking valve stops the recirculation the tests measured.

clueText.nc-a: Pump 2 and the running performance of Pump 1 do not support replacing pumps.
clueText.nc-b: A bigger wet well stores recirculated water but does not stop the waste.
clueText.nc-c: After the valve is replaced, the level holds steady after Pump 1 stops and run hours fall back.

tasks.prompt: One pump at a Kelowna lift station keeps losing prime performance and ragging, while its twin runs clean for months.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Pump 2 clogs with rags about every two weeks and Pump 1 beside it does not clog.
Inspection finds Pump 2 suction bell sitting in a corner dead zone where rags and grit collect.
Pump 1 suction sits in the main flow path and stays swept clean.
Both pumps are the same model, age and impeller type.
After the wet well is cleaned and a benching change guides flow past Pump 2 suction, clogging stops for three months.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Pump 2 impeller is defective from the factory
Residents on Pump 2 side of the street flush more wipes
The dead zone at Pump 2 suction collects rags that clog that pump, a layout problem rather than a pump defect
Pump 2 motor runs backward and pulls rags in

inference.explanation: Identical pumps, a collection corner at one suction, and a cure from a flow guiding change identify the wet well layout, not the machine or the residents.

nextClue.prompt: Which monitoring best confirms the layout fix over time?

options.label: Track clog events per pump in the station log and compare the twins over the next season
Assume the problem is solved and stop logging clogs
Test Pump 2 motor rotation monthly

nextClue.explanation: Comparing clog counts between identical twins is the direct test of the layout theory.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows zero Pump 2 clogs in the season after the change, matching Pump 1.
clueText.nc-b: Without a log there is no evidence the fix held.
clueText.nc-c: Rotation was never implicated, and the pump delivered normal flow when clear.

tasks.prompt: A Manitoba station spare impeller is installed during a repair, and the pump never reaches its former capacity afterward.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Before the repair the pump met its rated drawdown rate.
The installed spare impeller measures 25 mm smaller in diameter than the impeller removed.
Motor current after the repair is lower than before at the same speed and levels.
The volute, wear rings and discharge path are unchanged and in good condition.
Fitting the correct diameter impeller restores the original drawdown rate.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pump casing wore out during the short repair shutdown
The force main partly blocked at the same time as the repair
The motor lost a phase during the repair
The undersized spare impeller reduced the pump output, a parts mismatch rather than new wear

inference.explanation: A smaller impeller, lower current, sound casing, and full recovery with the correct part identify the parts mismatch. A blocked main would raise pressure and not be cured by an impeller swap.

nextClue.prompt: Which stores practice best prevents this repeat?

options.label: Order two of every spare so a wrong one is less likely
Tag spare rotating parts with measured diameter and pump model, and verify against the removed part at installation
Record only the part number and not the measurement

nextClue.explanation: Measured tagging catches mismatches that part numbers alone have already missed once.

clueText.nc-a: Doubling spares doubles the chance of picking the wrong one without a check.
clueText.nc-b: Spares are tagged with diameter and model, and the install step includes a compare check.
clueText.nc-c: The part number record existed during this event and did not prevent the mismatch.

tasks.prompt: A station in a prairie city passes its pump inspection with flying colours, yet station capacity stays low and head readings stay high.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Both pumps test at rated flow against a test header at the station.
Discharge pressure during normal operation is far above the station historic value.
Pigging the force main returns a heavy load of scale and tuberculation chunks.
After pigging, operating pressure falls to historic values and station capacity returns.
Force main age and water chemistry in the area are known for scale buildup.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Force main scale buildup raised the system head and cut station capacity, while the pumps were healthy
Both pumps lost efficiency in a way the test header cannot detect
The wet well shrank because of sediment and starved the station
The pressure gauge drifted and invented the high head

inference.explanation: Healthy pumps on a test header, high operating head, a heavy scale return, and recovery after pigging put the restriction in the force main, not the machines.

nextClue.prompt: Which program addition best manages this risk?

options.label: Replace the pumps whenever station capacity falls
Trust the pressure gauge less and stop trending pressure
Add periodic force main pressure trending with a pigging trigger when head rises above a set band

nextClue.explanation: Trending head catches scale growth early and times the cleaning that fixed it.

clueText.nc-a: Pump replacement was already disproven by the test header results.
clueText.nc-b: The gauge was confirmed by the recovery after pigging, so trending it is worthwhile.
clueText.nc-c: The station trend now flags a pigging review when operating head rises 15 percent over baseline.

tasks.prompt: A lift station pump in Edmonton shows rising vibration and bearing temperature over three weekly checks, though its flow is unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Vibration readings on the pump bearing housing roughly double over three weeks.
Bearing temperature climbs steadily and is now near the maker alarm value.
Drawdown flow and motor current remain at normal values.
Oil in the bearing housing is dark and contains fine metal particles.
The twin pump shows normal vibration, temperature and clean oil.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pump is losing hydraulic efficiency and needs an impeller
A developing bearing failure is the finding, a mechanical fault caught before it stops the pump
The force main is surging and shaking the pump
The vibration meter battery is weak and readings are drifting

inference.explanation: Normal hydraulics with rising vibration, heat, and metal in the oil of one pump only describe a bearing wearing out. The twin pump clears the shared force main and the meter method.

nextClue.prompt: Which action best fits a Class II reliability program?

options.label: Schedule a planned bearing replacement on the affected pump and keep the twin in service, rather than running to failure
Keep running the pump until it trips, to use its full life
Replace the impeller first and recheck vibration later

nextClue.explanation: A planned swap avoids an unplanned station outage from a failure already in progress.

clueText.nc-a: The bearing is replaced on a planned shift and vibration returns to the twin pump range.
clueText.nc-b: Running to failure risks a station outage and secondary damage to shaft and seals.
clueText.nc-c: Flow is normal, so the impeller is not the part the evidence points to.

tasks.prompt: A standby generator at a Saskatchewan lift station starts on its weekly test but the station still loses pumping during a real outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station performance test. Readings are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The generator engine starts and runs smoothly on every weekly no load test.
During a real outage the automatic transfer switch does not move to generator power.
Station batteries and the generator fuel supply test normal.
A manual transfer during a planned drill powers the pumps correctly from the generator.
The transfer switch shows a failed control relay on inspection after the outage.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The generator engine is too small for the station load
The station ran out of fuel during the outage
The transfer switch relay failure, not the generator, left the station unpowered during the outage
The pumps cannot run on generator power at all

inference.explanation: The engine runs, manual transfer powers the pumps, and a failed relay is found, so generation and load are fine and the automatic transfer path failed.

nextClue.prompt: Which test change best closes this gap?

options.label: Test the generator engine start more often each week
Add a regular loaded transfer test that runs the station on generator power, not just a no load engine start
Install a larger generator as a precaution

nextClue.explanation: Only a transfer test exercises the relay that actually failed.

clueText.nc-a: More engine starts still never move the transfer switch.
clueText.nc-b: Monthly drills now transfer the full station load and log relay operation.
clueText.nc-c: The generator powered the station fine on manual transfer, so size is not the issue.

tasks.prompt: CCTV in a Regina clay sewer shows a long crack running along the pipe with white staining and a steady trickle entering through it.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: A crack runs lengthwise for about 3 m in the pipe barrel.
White mineral staining borders the crack and a trickle of clear water enters through it during dry weather.
No displacement or missing pieces are seen at the crack.
Groundwater in the area stands above the pipe.
Reaches without cracks in the same run are dry inside.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A surface scratch from the camera crawler with no leak
Grease coating the pipe wall along a seam
A construction joint that was designed to weep
A structural barrel crack that is actively leaking groundwater into the pipe

inference.explanation: Length, mineral staining, a dry weather trickle, high groundwater, and dry sound reaches make this an active leaking crack, not a scratch or a designed feature.

nextClue.prompt: Which grading note best captures this defect for the rehabilitation list?

options.label: Record it as a minor surface mark with no action
Record it as a grease deposit for the cleaning program only
Record a leaking structural crack with active infiltration, with its length and chainage, for sealing or lining assessment

nextClue.explanation: An active leak through a structural crack belongs on the rehabilitation assessment list.

clueText.nc-a: Calling an actively leaking crack minor would drop a real I/I source from the program.
clueText.nc-b: Cleaning does not seal a cracked barrel.
clueText.nc-c: The log records the crack chainage, length and infiltration so the reach can be ranked for lining.

tasks.prompt: At one joint in a Winnipeg sewer the downstream pipe is shifted sideways, the gap is open, and dark soil is visible in the opening.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The joint is displaced sideways by about half the pipe wall thickness and more.
Soil is visible through the open joint gap.
Roots are absent at this joint, and flow passes without ponding above it.
A surface depression is developing in the lane above this chainage.
Joints upstream and downstream are aligned and tight.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A displaced open joint that is losing surrounding soil support, shown by the visible soil and surface depression
A normal flexible joint designed with a wide gap
A root blockage forming at the joint
A camera angle illusion with a sound joint below

inference.explanation: Displacement, visible soil, and a depression forming above form one picture of soil loss at a failed joint. Neighbouring joints show what a sound joint looks like in the same pipe.

nextClue.prompt: Which priority best fits this joint?

options.label: Rank it high for repair because soil loss can grow into a void and a road failure
Rank it low because flow still passes the joint
Rank it with routine cleaning defects

nextClue.explanation: Soil loss threatens the road above, not just the pipe, so it outranks defects that only affect flow.

clueText.nc-a: The joint is flagged high priority with the depression noted for the repair crew and road group.
clueText.nc-b: Flow passing today does not reduce the risk of a growing void.
clueText.nc-c: Cleaning cannot restore soil or realign a displaced joint.

tasks.prompt: CCTV in a flexible plastic sewer in Alberta shows the pipe squeezed into an oval, with the vertical diameter clearly reduced at one reach.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The pipe cross section is visibly oval over a 12 m reach, worst at its middle.
Measured vertical diameter is about 12 percent less than the nominal diameter.
No cracks or joint defects are seen in the oval reach.
The reach passes under a recently deepened road crossing with heavy truck traffic.
The same pipe material in a nearby park reach is round on camera.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Sediment on the invert is making the pipe look oval
The flexible pipe has deformed under surface loading, a structural shape defect rather than a blockage
The camera lens is distorting the picture in this reach only
Roots are squeezing the pipe from outside

inference.explanation: A measured diameter loss, a loaded crossing above, and round pipe of the same material nearby confirm true deformation. Sediment sits on the invert and does not change the crown shape.

nextClue.prompt: Which rehabilitation implication follows from the deformation?

options.label: Line it immediately, because a liner restores a round pipe
Assess it for replacement or re-rounding before any lining, since a liner follows the deformed shape
Jet it, because deformation is a deposit problem

nextClue.explanation: Lining a deformed pipe locks in the oval shape, so shape correction comes first.

clueText.nc-a: A liner takes the host pipe shape and cannot correct 12 percent ovality.
clueText.nc-b: The reach is flagged for excavation assessment and kept off the lining list until its shape is addressed.
clueText.nc-c: Jetting removes deposits, and no deposits are reported in this reach.

tasks.prompt: Hard crusty buildup rings a joint in a British Columbia sewer, and a sample of the crust fizzes in a drop of weak acid in the lab test the crew performs.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The buildup is hard, pale and crusty, thickest right at a joint.
A sample fizzes with acid, matching a mineral deposit rather than an organic one.
Clear water seeps through the same joint in dry weather.
No restaurants or food premises discharge to this reach.
Jetting chips off only a little of the crust and it regrows within a year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Hardened grease from food premises upstream
Concrete pipe material growing inward from the wall
Mineral encrustation deposited by infiltrating groundwater at the leaking joint
Ice forming inside the pipe at the joint

inference.explanation: Acid reaction, joint location, active seepage, and no food premises identify groundwater minerals. Grease is soft and organic, and ice would be seasonal and melt.

nextClue.prompt: Which fix addresses the cause rather than the symptom?

options.label: Jet the crust on a shorter cycle forever
Add the reach to the grease program
Seal the leaking joint to cut off the mineral bearing groundwater, with crust removal as part of the repair

nextClue.explanation: Stopping the seepage stops the mineral supply that builds the crust.

clueText.nc-a: Jetting alone was already shown to give only a year of relief.
clueText.nc-b: There are no food premises on the reach, so a grease program does not fit.
clueText.nc-c: The joint is scheduled for sealing, with regrowth checks added to the follow up camera run.

tasks.prompt: A camera run in a Saskatoon sewer passes a reach where water sits in the pipe at no flow, and sediment lies thick in the standing water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: At zero inflow, a 15 m reach holds standing water while reaches above and below drain dry.
Sediment depth is greatest inside the standing water reach.
Invert survey shows the reach falls slightly backward compared with the design grade.
Roots, grease and structural defects are absent on the run.
Jetting clears the sediment, but it rebuilds in the same reach within months.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The downstream trunk is surcharging and backing water into this reach at all times
Residents discharge sediment laden water that settles only here
The pipe is undersized and runs full even at low flow
A sag or belly from a grade loss is ponding water and trapping sediment in that reach

inference.explanation: Standing water at zero inflow with a surveyed backward grade isolates a sag. A downstream surcharge would also back up at high flow times and affect neighbouring reaches, and the survey gives the physical cause.

nextClue.prompt: Which program decision best fits a sag finding?

options.label: Treat it as a structural grade defect for repair assessment, and keep cleaning as an interim measure only
Increase jetting frequency as the permanent solution
Downsize the cleaning program because the reach self cleans

nextClue.explanation: A grade defect needs a structural decision, with cleaning only buying time.

clueText.nc-a: The reach goes on the repair assessment list and cleaning continues at an interim interval.
clueText.nc-b: Years of jetting already show sediment returning to the same ponded reach.
clueText.nc-c: A ponded reach traps sediment rather than self cleaning.

tasks.prompt: A lateral connection in a Calgary sewer sticks well into the main, and debris and wipes are snagged on it building a partial blockage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: One lateral pipe protrudes about a third of the main diameter into the flow.
Wipes and debris hang on the protruding end, narrowing the opening.
Other lateral connections on the run sit flush with the main wall.
The main barrel and joints are otherwise sound.
Clearing the snagged debris restores flow, but debris catches again at the same connection within weeks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The protruding lateral is the snag point causing the recurring partial blockage
A grease problem is coating the whole reach
The main is collapsing at the connection
Residents suddenly began flushing wipes only at this home

inference.explanation: A protruding end, debris caught exactly there, flush connections elsewhere, and rapid re-catching identify the protrusion as the cause rather than a change in resident behaviour.

nextClue.prompt: Which repair best removes the snag point?

options.label: Jet the reach more often as the permanent fix
Trim or reline the protruding connection flush with the main wall
Fine the homeowner for the wipes found

nextClue.explanation: Removing the protrusion removes the place debris catches.

clueText.nc-a: Jetting clears the symptom and the debris returns within weeks, as already observed.
clueText.nc-b: The connection is scheduled for robotic trimming with a camera check after.
clueText.nc-c: Wipes appear throughout systems, and they only build a blockage here because of the protrusion.

tasks.prompt: CCTV at a river crossing sewer in Manitoba finds a section with several fractures, a missing piece of wall, and a dark void beyond the pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Multiple fractures cross the pipe wall in several directions over a 2 m section.
A piece of the wall is missing and a dark void is visible beyond the pipe.
Soil coloured water enters through the damaged section in dry weather.
The road above shows early settlement cracks over the same chainage.
Sections on both sides of the damage are in fair condition.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A minor defect that can wait for the next 10 year inspection cycle
An advanced local structural failure with soil loss, needing prompt repair rather than routine monitoring
A camera lighting effect that looks like a void
A designed access opening in the pipe wall

inference.explanation: Missing wall, void, soil entry, and surface settlement together describe failure in progress. Sound sections beside it rule out a picture effect and show the damage is local.

nextClue.prompt: Which response best matches the severity?

options.label: File it with the routine defect list for annual review
Clean the section and re-inspect in five years
Escalate it for prompt excavation and repair planning, with the crossing consequence noted

nextClue.explanation: Prompt action matches a failure that is already losing soil beside a crossing.

clueText.nc-a: Annual review leaves a growing void under a road for another year.
clueText.nc-b: Cleaning does not repair fractures or a missing wall.
clueText.nc-c: The section is escalated the same week with settlement monitoring started above it.

tasks.prompt: The crown of a concrete sewer below a drop manhole in Edmonton is rough, soft in places, and the steel reinforcement is showing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CCTV inspection, defects described in generic condition terms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Damage is worst at the crown, above the water line, and fades lower on the walls.
The drop manhole above creates turbulent flow that releases sewer gas at this reach.
Hydrogen sulfide readings in the manhole are high.
The invert concrete is hard and in good condition.
Similar crown damage appears at other turbulent drop locations in the system.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Flow abrasion is wearing the crown away from the top down
Roots are dissolving the concrete crown
Sulfide driven corrosion is attacking the crown concrete where gas is released at the turbulent drop
The pipe was made with thin concrete at the crown only

An assessment of re-rounding or open cut renewal for the deformed reach, with lining kept for reaches inside the limit
A note to increase resin quantity to fill the oval shape

A general statement that wipes are bad for sewers
The rainfall record for the overflow day

tasks.prompt: A sewer in a growing Alberta suburb overflows weeks after road construction above it, and the timing points the investigation.

tasks.prompt: Crown corrosion is found in a concrete sewer just downstream of a drop structure in a Manitoba town, and the odour program reviews the pattern.

tasks.prompt: Odour complaints at a force main discharge in Edmonton arrive in bursts that match the station pumping pattern.

Residents cannot tell storm from sanitary structures, so the case is closed
A sanitary overflow occurred into the storm system that week

inference.explanation: Structure by structure checks put the smell on storm basins full of decaying sediment, with a clean sanitary system and relief after basin cleaning. Resident confusion was resolved by measurement, not dismissal.

nextClue.prompt: Which handover best closes the case?

options.label: Add the street to the sanitary odour dosing program
Tell residents the odour is imaginary
Pass the catch basin cleaning need to the storm program with the sediment findings, and record the sanitary system as checked and clear

nextClue.explanation: Routing the finding to the program that owns the source gets it fixed.

clueText.nc-a: Dosing a clear sanitary sewer treats nothing and spends the odour budget wrongly.

The odour is normal sewer gas that residents describe oddly
An industrial discharge is the odour source, not the sulfide program usual target
The solvent smell comes from road paving somewhere in the city

Refer the discharge to the sewer use and source control review for that premises, with the odour timing log attached
Tell residents the readings prove there is no odour

clueText.nc-a: Dosing targets sulfide generation, which readings show is low here.
clueText.nc-b: The file goes to source control with production hour odour logs and the solvent change notice.

tasks.prompt: A wet well vent stack in a prairie town draws odour complaints from homes right beside it, while a taller stack across town draws none.

Residents near this station complain more readily than others
The vent fan at this station is oversized
Poor dispersion from the short vent is the complaint driver, not stronger sewage at this station

Ask the neighbours to keep windows closed permanently
Raise or relocate the vent discharge to improve dispersion away from the neighbouring homes

clueText.nc-a: Dosing may help sulfide but the twin station shows dispersion, not strength, is the difference.
clueText.nc-b: Window advice leaves a fixable design issue in place.
clueText.nc-c: The vent is scheduled for a height extension with complaint tracking after the change.

tasks.prompt: A scrubber at a large Alberta lift station passes its media check, yet odour at the vent stays strong, and an airflow inspection follows.

The media is exhausted despite its test result
The station sewage strength doubled that month
The vent samples were taken incorrectly all month

inference.explanation: Active media, a found open bypass, measured bypass flow, and recovery after repair form a complete chain. Media exhaustion contradicts its own test result.

nextClue.prompt: Which maintenance item belongs on the scrubber checklist?

options.label: A damper position and airflow path check at every scrubber service, alongside the media test
Media replacement at double the current frequency
A second sulfide meter to double check every reading

clueText.nc-a: Scrubber services now include damper position verification with the airflow split recorded.
clueText.nc-b: Doubling media changes does nothing for air that never reaches the media.
clueText.nc-c: The meter agreed with the repair result, so it was not the problem.

tasks.prompt: A shallow home service in a Saskatchewan town freezes in a severe cold week after the street snow was cleared down to bare pavement.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cold climate operations case. Temperatures, depths and dates are as stated.

evidence.label: The service pipe lies at shallow cover for its area, known from records.
Snow clearing removed the insulating snow layer over the service that week.
Neighbouring deeper services on the same street do not freeze.
The same service survived milder winters with snow left in place.
No flow or blockage problem is found in the service after thawing.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The service pipe collapsed during the cold week
Frost reached the shallow service because its snow insulation was removed during extreme cold
The home used too little water that week by coincidence
The main sewer froze and blocked the service

inference.explanation: Shallow cover, snow removal, surviving deep neighbours, and a sound pipe after thaw identify frost penetration. A collapse would not thaw back to normal.

nextClue.prompt: Which winter practice best protects shallow services?

options.label: Excavate every service on the street before next winter
Leave or replace insulating snow cover over known shallow services during extreme cold, and list them for monitoring
Tell homeowners to run taps all winter as the only measure

nextClue.explanation: Protecting the known shallow services targets the mechanism at low cost.

clueText.nc-a: Excavating sound, deeper services is not supported by their survival.
clueText.nc-b: Shallow services are mapped and snow handling notes added for cold snaps.
clueText.nc-c: Running taps helps some cases but the recorded cause was lost ground insulation.

tasks.prompt: Ice builds on the walls of a Manitoba lift station wet well each winter, thickest around the vent pipe opening.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cold climate operations case. Temperatures, depths and dates are as stated.

evidence.label: Ice growth is worst on the wall beside the vent pipe entry.
The vent draws cold outside air across the wet well surface in winter.
The wet well heater works, but its thermostat is mounted in the warmest corner.
A sister station with an insulated, baffled vent shows little ice.
Ice melts back each spring with no structural damage found.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

The pumps are splashing sewage that freezes in layers
Cold air drawn through the vent is chilling the wet well locally, and the heater control does not sense that cold zone
The whole station heating system has failed

inference.explanation: Ice localised at the vent, a working heater with a badly placed sensor, and a baffled twin station identify cold air entry, not leakage or total heating failure.

nextClue.prompt: Which fix best matches the cold zone finding?

options.label: Install a much larger heater for the whole station
Seal the vent completely for the winter
Insulate and baffle the vent path and move the heater thermostat to sense the cold zone

nextClue.explanation: Treating the air path and the sensing point addresses the local chill directly.

clueText.nc-a: A bigger heater controlled from the warm corner still misses the cold zone.
clueText.nc-b: Sealing a wet well vent entirely creates gas and pressure problems.
clueText.nc-c: The vent is baffled and the thermostat relocated, with ice checks added to winter rounds.

tasks.prompt: An air release valve on a northern Alberta force main is found frozen and split after a cold snap, with a small sewage leak at the site.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cold climate operations case. Temperatures, depths and dates are as stated.

evidence.label: The valve body holds water in a low pocket that does not drain back.
Temperatures fell below minus 30 degrees Celsius for several nights before the leak.
The valve chamber insulation was damaged and partly missing.
Other valves on the main with intact insulation and drained bodies are undamaged.
The force main pipe itself pressure tests sound after the valve is isolated.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

The valve was defective from manufacture
Ground movement in the cold snap crushed the chamber
Water trapped in the uninsulated valve body froze and split it, a cold protection failure at that chamber

nextClue.prompt: Which program step best prevents the next split?

options.label: Add chamber insulation checks and valve drain down confirmation to the fall winterisation round
Replace every air valve on the main each fall
Raise force main operating pressure for winter

nextClue.explanation: Winterisation checks target exactly the conditions that failed.

clueText.nc-a: Air valve chambers join the fall checklist with insulation and drainage items signed off.

clueText.nc-c: Higher pressure adds stress and does nothing against freezing.

tasks.prompt: Winter flow monitoring in a prairie basin returns long data gaps, and the spring review examines the logger records.

The sensor itself passes its spring bench test.
A logger fitted with a cold rated battery pack and insulation records through the next cold snap without gaps.
No sewer flow anomaly is recorded by a nearby station logger on the gap nights.

The sewer ran dry on the coldest nights
The sensor iced over and blocked all readings
Someone switched the loggers off on cold nights

inference.explanation: Voltage records, temperature timing, a sound sensor, and a cold rated pack succeeding identify the power supply in cold, a classic winter monitoring trap.

nextClue.prompt: Which specification belongs in the winter monitoring plan?

options.label: Deploy the same warm weather kits and accept winter gaps
Specify cold rated batteries and insulated logger housings for winter deployments, with voltage alarms
Move all flow monitoring to summer only

nextClue.explanation: Cold rated kit keeps the winter record the I/I program needs.

clueText.nc-a: Accepting gaps loses exactly the freeze and thaw data the program studies.
clueText.nc-b: Winter deployments now list cold rated packs and a low voltage alarm check.
clueText.nc-c: Summer only data cannot show snowmelt or freeze season behaviour.

tasks.prompt: A spring problem appears in a Manitoba town: sewer infiltration is low all winter, then jumps sharply during the spring thaw.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cold climate operations case. Temperatures, depths and dates are as stated.

Night flow climbs steeply over the two weeks when frost leaves the ground.
Groundwater levels rise sharply during the same thaw window.
CCTV after thaw shows joints weeping that were dry on a winter run.
A basin on sandy high ground shows a much smaller thaw jump.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Thaw released groundwater drives the spring infiltration jump, a seasonal pattern the program must plan around
Residents discharge more water every spring by habit
The winter flow meter was frozen and under reading

inference.explanation: Frozen ground suppressing infiltration, a thaw timed rise with groundwater, and weeping joints after thaw describe seasonal groundwater release. The winter rain event with low response rules out rain alone.

nextClue.prompt: Which scheduling decision best uses this pattern?

options.label: Schedule all CCTV in mid winter when pipes are driest
Cancel groundwater monitoring because the pattern is seasonal
Schedule infiltration assessment CCTV during the high groundwater thaw window, when leaks are active and visible

clueText.nc-a: Winter runs already showed dry joints in a basin that leaks heavily in spring.
clueText.nc-b: Groundwater data is what predicted the active window, so it stays in the program.

tasks.prompt: Manholes along a ploughed Alberta street are found in spring with frames lifted and tilted, and infiltration has started at the frame joints.

The frames were installed tilted the previous summer
Frost heave lifted the uninsulated street frames, opening the joints that now leak
Traffic loads increased enough to tilt the frames in one winter

options.label: Reseat and reseal the heaved frames and restore insulating cover depth where the design allows
Replace the manhole barrels below the frames
Only sweep the street so the frames look level

tasks.prompt: A small diameter pressure pipe at a Saskatchewan station bursts during a cold snap, and the station heating record is reviewed.

A sister station with a working heater alarm had its failure attended within hours and no freeze damage.

The record cold alone explains it, with the heater playing no part
The unnoticed heater failure let a still, small line freeze and burst during record cold

Test heater failure alarms on the station round and add a low temperature alarm as a backup
Replace all small pipes in every station

clueText.nc-b: Heater and low temperature alarms join the monthly tested list with call out verification.

tasks.prompt: Winter jetting in a Manitoba town leaves the street icy at each manhole, and the safety review examines the cleaning method.

Trial blocks using the vacuum show no ice sheet forming.
No pipe cleaning quality difference is found between the methods.

Residents are spilling water that freezes on those streets
The town should simply stop cleaning sewers in winter
Colder water from the jetting truck is the whole problem

inference.explanation: Trial blocks isolate capture as the difference, with cleaning quality unchanged. Stopping winter cleaning entirely would trade a manageable hazard for blockages.

nextClue.prompt: Which winter procedure best follows the trial?

options.label: Sand every street after jetting and keep the old method
Clean only on warm winter days above freezing
Require downstream vacuum capture for winter jetting and record surface ice checks on the job sheet

nextClue.explanation: Capture prevents the ice rather than treating it afterwards.

clueText.nc-a: Sanding treats ice after it forms and leaves the spreading water unaddressed.
clueText.nc-b: Warm days are rare in the season when some cleaning cannot wait.
clueText.nc-c: The winter procedure adopts vacuum capture with an ice check sign off.

tasks.prompt: A frozen outfall in a northern town backs up the end of a sewer each late winter, then clears suddenly at thaw.

At thaw, flow clears suddenly and levels normalise within a day.
A second outfall on a deeper, faster creek reach nearby does not freeze shut.

The creek is flooding back into the sewer all winter
Roots grow shut each winter and die each spring

inference.explanation: Ice at the outfall, sound upstream pipe, sudden thaw clearing, and an unfrozen comparison outfall identify creek ice. A debris blockage would show on camera as material, not ice at the end.

nextClue.prompt: Which monitoring best manages a known freezing outfall?

options.label: Add late winter level checks at the last manhole, with a thaw watch, for the outfalls known to freeze
Line the last reach of sewer each decade
Jet the last reach monthly all winter

nextClue.explanation: Level checks catch the backup building before it reaches homes.

tasks.prompt: Snowmelt ponds over a parking lot in a prairie city each spring, and sanitary flows from the block spike while the lot is flooded.

A neighbouring block with raised manhole covers shows no melt flow spike.

Meltwater is entering through the low manhole covers ponded in the lot

nextClue.prompt: Which lot level fix best fits the finding?

Raise and seal the two manhole covers above the ponding depth, or regrade the lot corner so water no longer ponds there
Ban snow storage on the lot as the only measure

tasks.prompt: A duplex station in Calgary logs far more pump starts per day than its design, and the motors are heating on short runs.

Pump capacity and wet well size match the design drawings.

nextClue.prompt: Which setting record belongs in the station file?

Narrow the range further to keep levels tighter
Record the approved start and stop levels and the resulting starts per day, so future changes are visible

tasks.prompt: Run time records at a British Columbia duplex station show the lead pump doing about 90 percent of the work for a full quarter.

The lead pump is more efficient and the controls prefer it

nextClue.prompt: Which check belongs on the station round?

options.label: Compare pump run hours at each visit and investigate any growing imbalance between the pair
Record only total station run hours
Swap pump names in the log so the hours look balanced

nextClue.explanation: Run hour balance is an early warning for exactly this silent failure.

tasks.prompt: Pressure logging on a force main in Edmonton shows a sharp spike every time a station pump stops, and joints along the main have begun to weep.

Adopt controlled pump stop sequencing and trend the spike height, with joint inspections while it settles
Ignore the spikes because steady pressure is normal

tasks.prompt: A force main flow balance in a prairie city shows pumped volume exceeding plant arrival volume by a growing margin over three months.

nextClue.prompt: Which monitoring best catches the next leak earlier?

options.label: Wait for surface evidence before investigating any imbalance
Check meter calibration only, every five years
Trend the station to plant flow balance monthly with a set investigation trigger on the gap

clueText.nc-b: Calibration was not the fault here, and five years is too long an interval for this check.

tasks.prompt: A standby generator at a Manitoba station runs the building lights on test but stalls when the large pump tries to start on generator power.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station reliability and records case. Logs and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: The generator carries lights and small loads without trouble.

Utility power starts the same pump normally every day.
A soft starter fitted in a trial lets the pump start smoothly on generator power.
Generator engine condition and fuel test normal, and its rating suits the running load.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The generator is simply too small for the station in all respects
The pump motor is failing and draws excess current at all times
The fuel quality is causing the stalls at pump start
Pump starting current, not running load, exceeds what the generator can deliver at start, and soft starting fixes it

inference.explanation: Normal utility starts, a healthy engine, and a successful soft start trial isolate the starting surge. A failing motor would misbehave on utility power too.

nextClue.prompt: Which specification matters at the next generator review?

options.label: State the largest motor starting requirement alongside running load in the standby power specification
Specify running load only, since that is the steady demand
Remove the large pump from the generator circuit

nextClue.explanation: Standby sizing that ignores starting current repeats this failure.

clueText.nc-a: The station power review now lists motor starting demand beside running load.
clueText.nc-b: Running load alone was the basis that left starting unexamined.
clueText.nc-c: Removing the main pump defeats the purpose of standby power at a lift station.

tasks.prompt: An overflow at a Saskatchewan station is reported three days late, and the review finds the alarm call out list still names a retired operator first.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station reliability and records case. Logs and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: The alarm dialer called the retired operator number first and cycled slowly through old numbers.
The overflow itself was caused by a brief power dip and cleared when power returned.
Station staff learned of the event from a resident, not from the alarm system.
The call list had not been reviewed since the retirement, over a year earlier.
Current staff numbers work when dialled directly in a test after the event.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Outdated alarm call out information delayed the response and the reporting, a records maintenance failure
The alarm dialer hardware failed completely
Staff ignored the alarm calls they received
The power dip lasted three days and prevented any response

inference.explanation: A working dialer calling stale numbers, staff learning from a resident, and working current numbers on test identify the list, not the hardware or the staff, as the failure.

nextClue.prompt: Which routine best protects reporting timelines under general provincial requirements?

options.label: Review the list when the next late report happens
Review and test the alarm call list on a set schedule, with the test logged, and after every staff change
Add more numbers to the list without removing old ones

nextClue.explanation: Scheduled testing keeps the first call going to someone who can act.

clueText.nc-a: Waiting for the next failure repeats a known weakness.
clueText.nc-b: Call list tests join the quarterly routine and follow every staffing change.
clueText.nc-c: Keeping retired numbers ahead of current ones preserves the delay.

tasks.prompt: Level readings at an Alberta station drift slowly upward over weeks, while a staff gauge in the wet well shows the true level unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station reliability and records case. Logs and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: The electronic level reading climbs about 5 percent per week with no change in inflow pattern.
Staff gauge readings taken at the same times stay steady and match pump cycling.
Pump starts per day stay constant, matching the staff gauge, not the drifting signal.
Cleaning the sensor does not change the drift.
A bench test of the sensor shows an output offset that grows with operating time.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The wet well is slowly filling because inflow is rising
The level sensor itself is drifting and needs replacement, while the true level is normal
Sediment is raising the wet well floor week by week
The staff gauge is stuck and reading low

inference.explanation: Two independent witnesses, pump cycling and the staff gauge, agree against the sensor, and the bench test finds its growing offset. Inflow rise would change pump cycling, which stayed constant.

nextClue.prompt: Which practice limits the damage from a drifting sensor?

options.label: Trust the electronic reading alone because it is newer technology
Remove the staff gauge to avoid conflicting records
Keep an independent level check, such as the staff gauge, on the station round and compare it with the electronic reading

nextClue.explanation: An independent check is what caught this drift before it caused an event.

clueText.nc-a: Trusting the drifting signal alone would eventually misrun the station.
clueText.nc-b: Removing the gauge removes the comparison that worked.
clueText.nc-c: The round now logs both readings with a difference flag for investigation.

tasks.prompt: A wet well in a Winnipeg station grows a deep solids deposit in one corner, and the pump above that corner rags far more than its twin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station reliability and records case. Logs and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Solids depth in the corner reaches about half a metre between cleanings.
Flow entering the well shoots across the top and leaves the corner almost still.
The twin pump suction sits in the moving stream and stays clean.
Both pumps are identical and pass capacity tests after cleaning.
A trial baffle that sweeps flow through the corner keeps it clear for two cleaning cycles.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The corner pump is defective and attracts rags
Residents above that corner flush different material
A dead zone in the wet well is depositing solids that rag the corner pump, a hydraulics layout issue
The cleaning crew skips the corner on purpose

inference.explanation: Identical pumps, a still corner, and a baffle trial that keeps it clear identify flow pattern, not the pump, the residents, or the crew.

nextClue.prompt: Which design note belongs in the station record?

options.label: Record the dead zone and the baffle result so future wet well work keeps the sweep through the corner
Replace the corner pump with a larger model
Clean the corner weekly forever without changing the layout

nextClue.explanation: Recording the fix protects it when the well is next modified.

clueText.nc-a: The station file notes the baffle and the clear corner result across two cycles.
clueText.nc-b: A larger pump in a dead zone still sits in deposited solids.
clueText.nc-c: Weekly cleaning was the cost the baffle trial just removed.

tasks.prompt: Several air release valves along a British Columbia force main are found fouled at the same inspection, and station pressure has been creeping up for months.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian lift station reliability and records case. Logs and test results are as stated.

evidence.label: Four of six air valves along the main are fouled shut or partly shut.
Station operating pressure has risen gradually over the same months.
Venting the high points manually drops operating pressure noticeably.
The valves had no scheduled service interval in the maintenance system.
Pumps test at rated performance against the test header.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: All four valves failed independently in the same month by chance
The force main is scaling shut along its whole length
The pumps are declining in step with the pressure rise
Unserviced air valves let air accumulate and raise the force main head, a missing maintenance program rather than pump decline

inference.explanation: Healthy pumps, fouled valves with no service history, and pressure relief on manual venting identify the missing valve program. Chance failure of four unserviced valves is the program gap itself.

nextClue.prompt: Which program entry closes this gap?

options.label: Replace all air valves with new ones and add no schedule
Create a scheduled air valve service task with an interval and a pressure trend review for the main
Add the pressure rise to the pump rebuild justification

nextClue.explanation: New valves without a schedule foul again on the same timeline.

clueText.nc-a: Replacing parts without the missing schedule repeats the root cause.
clueText.nc-b: Air valves enter the maintenance system with a service interval and pressure trending.
clueText.nc-c: Pump tests already cleared the pumps in this case.
